verdict.rationale: Modal Sandboxes are built to be driven programmatically. The Python SDK covers creating sandboxes, running exec commands, networking and resource parameters, snapshots and logs, and there is an official CLI for managing containers. Nothing documents that the API matches everything the UI can do, and the JS/Go SDKs cover only 'some Modal platform resources'. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement or a complete API reference (no OpenAPI spec found), full platform-resource coverage in all SDKs, and independent confirmation that UI-only actions do not exist.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Spin up fresh, isolated sandboxes programmatically.
A `Sandbox` object lets you interact with a running sandbox.
We've added a modal.Sandbox.logs API, allowing you to fetch() logs from a specific date/time range or to tail() the most recent logs.
Manage and connect to running containers.
The JS and Go SDKs allow you to use Modal Sandboxes, invoke deployed Modal Functions, and interact with some Modal platform resources.
